import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot using seaborn
# Petal measurements generally show better separation between species than sepal measurements
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=100,  # size of the markers
    alpha=0.8, # transparency
    palette='viridis' # color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Species', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Improve layout and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot using seaborn
# Petal measurements generally show better separation between species than sepal measurements
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=100,  # size of the markers
    alpha=0.8, # transparency
    palette='viridis' # color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Species', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Improve layout and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
